chunks: And there is a man who is willing to sell even his soul to win the favour of God; and God is compassionate to His creatures.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to sell one's soul for the sake of God's pleasure?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the ultimate sacrifice of Imam al-Husayn (AS) at Karbala, who 'sold' his life to revive the Sunnah of his grandfather. The phrase 'Allah is Kind to the servants' (Ra'uf) emphasizes that this voluntary self-sacrifice is not a loss but a divine transaction secured by God's mercy, distinguishing it from mere martyrdom.
